contracts.overview:
High-frequency payment systems face microsecond cache bottlenecks when thousands of transaction auth tokens expire concurrently. You must implement the function cacheResolver(entries, threshold) to filter out expired items and return remaining entries sorted by priority.

### Deliverables
1. Deterministic memory cache filter and priority sorter.
2. Sub-millisecond execution complexity bounded by O(N log N).
3. Zero secret exposure and strict input boundary validation.

rules.judgingConduct: Judges' and Kilikoro Autonomous AST Oracle decisions are final. BMONI milestone escrow is automatically released to the verified submitter's virtual card in under 3 seconds upon passing.
rules.aiPolicy: You are allowed full use of AI tools, coding assistants, and open-source packages. All code is audited against AST security trees and anti-hallucination entropy checks.
rules.teamSize: Teams may have 1 to 5 members. Solo submissions are fully welcomed. Each team may submit only one primary solution repository.
rules.eligibility: Open to all middle school, high school, polytechnic, and undergraduate students (ages 13 to 25) enrolled in NACOS chapters or international student developer networks.
rules.submissionRules: Submissions must not contain offensive, harmful, or plagiarized content. Secrets, live private keys, and exposed API tokens will trigger instant AST audit failure.

audits.summary: BuildX-Crown-Chasers is a Kilikoro developer verification & escrow platform with clean security posture and solid documentation, but the codebase shows incomplete error handling patterns and frontend-heavy architecture lacking backend resilience validation. The project demonstrates competent UI/UX design and framework understanding, though production readiness is hindered by missing network error handlers and edge-case coverage.
strengths: Zero exposed secrets or credentials in static scan
Modern HTML5/CSS structure with responsive viewport configuration and semantic accessibility markers
Modular sidebar navigation pattern and SaaS-grade UI layout design
Quality score of 92 from static analysis indicates above-average code cleanliness
hygieneFlags: Sample code provided is HTML/CSS only—no backend validation logic, API integration code, or Node.js/TypeScript implementation visible to verify claimed 'Node.js/TypeScript' competency
Missing error boundary patterns: no try-catch blocks visible in provided snippet; onclick handlers (e.g., `app.switchView()`) lack null-safety guards
No evidence of API error handling (timeouts, 5xx responses, malformed JSON) despite claim of 'API Integrations'
Frontend-centric repo structure (js/, css/, assets/) suggests single-page application without visible backend architecture—inconsistent with 'Software Engineering' breadth claims
MEMORY.TXT and DOWNLOADS.TXT files suggest development scraps not cleaned before commit
No unit tests, integration tests, or test configuration visible—high-risk for production without test coverage proof
Hardcoded view IDs ('view-verifier', 'view-contracts') and inline styles indicate potential maintainability debt
verifiedClaims: Modern Frameworks: Codebase uses semantic HTML5, modular CSS structure (claude-theme.css), and organized component layout suggesting framework awareness
Data Structures: Navigation patterns and state management (sidebar nav, contract counter badges) indicate understanding of UI state organization
Software Engineering: Technical documentation files (SYSTEM_ENGINEERING_SPECIFICATION.md, MASTER_TECHNICAL_REPORT.md) demonstrate specification-driven design thinking
unverifiedClaims: Node.js/TypeScript: No .ts files, package.json, or backend code visible; provided sample is pure HTML/CSS
API Integrations: Sample code references `app.switchView()` but no fetch(), axios, or HTTP client calls visible; no API endpoint definitions found in provided files
Data Structures: Claims lack evidence of complex algorithmic structures or backend data modeling (no server-side validation, caching, or database schemas evidenced)

technicalNotes.architectureObservations: Single-page application with event-driven view switching (onclick handlers bound to app object). Architecture is frontend-forward; backend API layer not visible in provided context. Sidebar navigation and contract escrow module suggest feature-complete product design but lack production-grade separation of concerns.
riskFactors: No visible error handling for network latency, API failures, or user input validation
Escrow contract logic handling financial/milestone data without visible cryptographic or transaction safety patterns
Missing CSRF tokens, Content Security Policy, or SameSite cookie attributes in sample HTML
technicalNotes.recommendedReview: Request full backend codebase (kilikoro.js should contain app initialization and API logic—review its error handling, validation, and external API calls). Require unit test suite and load-testing results. Verify claims around Node.js/TypeScript expertise with actual backend code or prior project examples.
